summary: Forest Service lookout on Pine Mountain east of Bend, rebuilt in 1932 and removed by 1968. A university observatory now stands on the mountain.

facts.status_note: Removed by 1968. No source describes what remains of the lookout on the summit today.

visit.trail_note: Hikers can walk the ridge from the University of Oregon observatory to the true summit. The observatory is open to the public on Friday and Saturday nights on 7 to 10 weekends from May through September.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives a 41-foot L-4 tower in 1951; the Oregon lookout history gives a 28-foot CT-2 tower with an L-4 cab in 1952. The 28-foot figure is about 8.5 m, which matches the record's height_m, so the record's height may describe the later tower.
The Morning Oregonian (Oct. 9, 1929) says Putnam was in the tower; the Bend Bulletin (Oct. 8, 1929) says he was resting on his bed. The story reports both and does not choose.

sources.title: Pine Mountain Lookout Site (US 1033), Former Fire Lookout Sites Register
Pine Mountain, Forest Lookouts of Oregon

notes_for_editor: The 1921 cabin and 1932 tower agree across the register and firelookout.com. The replacement tower differs: 1951 and 41 ft (register) against 1952 and 28 ft (Oregon history). The record's height_m of 8.5 m matches only the 28-foot tower. firelookout.com's span of 1921-1951 conflicts with removal by 1968 in the other two sources; the story reports both. The record point is roughly 3 km from the summit coordinates on Wikipedia (43.8031, -120.9134), so the sources do not place the lookout on the observatory summit and the story does not. One web search found no source on the site's current condition. No access level is given for the lookout site itself, so none is recorded. Photos were not fetched or added. Verification 2026-10-09: the 1929 lightning account conflicts between two newspapers, so the story now reports both; the 1932 fire is described as in the 1930 Big Springs burn, as the source says; the campground is now quoted with its Forest Service label.
